subject: DSsim: Setting detectability using adjusment or covariates

messages.author: fa112d5a5313e536
messages.subject: DSsim: Setting detectability using adjusment or covariates
parts:
Dear Listserv,

Is it possible to create a detectability object in DSsim which is based on a Uniform + adjustment term (scale parameter is 0 + adjustment terms) or define a detection function (hazard rate) which included scale coefficients from covariates? I believe it is not possible through the <make.detectability> function, but might be missing something.

Many thanks for any pointers and your time.

Regards,

Don

messages.author: d6a29bde56bb826d
messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re: {Disarmed} [distance-sampling] DSsim: Setting detectability using adjusment or covariates
parts:
Dear Don,



You are correct in that you cannot define adjustment terms in the make.detectability function to specify the detection function used to generate the data. However, you can define a hazard rate detection function where the scale parameter is affected by covariates. Please find an example below where the scale parameter varies with cluster size.


library(DSsim)
covariate.list <- list()
covariate.list$size <- list(list("ztruncpois", list(mean = 5)))
pop <- make.population.description(covariates = covariate.list)

covariate.params <- list(size = 0.1)
detect <- make.detectability(key.function = 'hr',
                             shape.param = 1,
                             cov.param = covariate.params)

plot(detect, pop)

Best wishes,


Laura

parts:
Dear Laura,

Thank you for the explanation and time. I was hoping to use a detection function I obtained from a survey in a simulation, but have not been able successfully implement this as yet. My apologies for a probably somewhat basic question.

I have the following detection function parameters from a half normal:

Detection function parameters
Scale coefficient(s):  
                         estimate        se
(Intercept)             5.7116050 0.2145045
observerTK             -0.2659522 0.2450585
speedlow               -0.3265619 0.2450650

Both observer and speed are factors.

The below code works for me but would this be the correct way to set up the detection, in particular the cov.params objects parameters based on a modelled detection function output?

covariate.list <- list()
covariate.list$observer <- list(data.frame(level = c("TK", "JAH"), prob = c(0.5,0.5)))
covariate.list$speed <- list(data.frame(level = c("high", "low"), prob = c(0.5,0.5)))

pop.desc <- make.population.description(region.obj = region,
                                        density.obj = density,
                                        covariates = covariate.list,
                                        N = 1000)

cov.params <- list(speed = data.frame(level = c("low", "high"), param = c(-0.36, 1)),
                   observer = data.frame(level = c("TK", "JAH"),param = c(-0.26, 1)))


detect <- make.detectability(key.function = 'hn',
                             shape.param = exp(model$ddf$par[1]), #to get back to natural scale
                             cov.param = cov.params,
                             truncation = 150)


Many thanks again for your patience and help. Much appreciated.

Kind regards,

Don
